messages:
maria: seeing a steady uptick in preempt-driven evictions in us-west2c starting ~10:20. Kubernetes evict logs + node NIC errors. Pods are tiny-gang (0.5GPU-ish) churny ML training jobs.

akshay: any graphs? is it bandwidth vs nvlink/peerlink?

maria: attaching quick snippet from node dmesg (paste):

```
[ 1023.345678] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0 enp197s0f0: TX queue 0 stalled, restart
[ 1023.345930] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0 enp197s0f1: link down
[ 1023.346120] kernel: rmmod: can't remove mlx5_core: device busy
```

maria: and scheduler logs show a lot of evict -> requeue -> preempt loops for pods with small gang affinity.

jon: this smells like slot fragmentation + NIC saturating when pods land across the rack boundary. tiny-gang packing spreads them out, then backfill moves them, ping-pong.

ellie: agree. We saw similar last month but then fixed with warm-pool tuning. Is this only us-west2c?

maria: yes only us-west2c AZC. us-west2a/b normal. network metrics show ephemeral connection spikes across top-of-rack switches in that AZ.

akshay: quick mitigation: can we mark a soft-affinity to keep tiny-gang pods within the same rack or avoid cross-nic placements? perhaps use scheduler score plugin with rack-local weight.

jon: +1. Also we can temporary throttle preemptive backfill for pods with <1GPU to reduce churn. Add a short preempt budget: "preemptBudget: 5%" for small pods.

ellie: can we deploy these as a canary policy? don't want global scheduling changes. Maybe label the workload team with nodeAffinityPriority=localrack for a week.

maria: plan proposed: 1) apply a scheduler policy change in staging to weight rack-localness for pods with label "tiny-gang=true" 2) update autoscaler to avoid cross-rack warm-pool fills in AZC 3) throttle preempt backfill for <1GPU pods 4) monitor for 2 hours 5) rollback if unaffected.

akshay: OK to try. Maria can you paste the scheduler score snippet you had?

maria: snippet (kube-scheduler ext):

```
- name: RackLocality
  args:
    weight: 30
    whenPodLabel: "tiny-gang=true"
```

maria: I know it's rough but low-risk canary in us-west2c only. We'll patch scheduler config on the two scheduler replicas in that region.

jon: add a metric alert: if evictions drop < 50% after 30m, we keep. If node NIC err rate doesn't improve, roll back and open network ENG ticket.

ellie: I'll prepare a quick playbook for rollback and kubectl commands.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0453 "us-west2c tiny-gang evict + NIC spike" assigned to eng-platform.

maria: rolling the canary in 5m. will post go/no-go. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy started: scheduler-config/us-west2c-canary (2 replicas) by maria at 1755000180

maria: go — canary live. watching metrics.

maria: 10m update: eviction rate down ~42%, NIC error spikes reduced but still occasional blips.

jon: promising. keep throttling preempt backfill for small pods for 1 hour and observe.

ellie: prepping PR to make RackLocality pluggable by label + default weight 0. will request review.

maria: 40m update: evictions down 61%, node NIC errors back to baseline. marking as partial success, will extend canary to 6h and then roll to other AZ if stable.

akshay: nice work. follow-up items: 1) long-term: scheduler should consider NIC topology (peerlink islands) in packing heuristic 2) autoscaler warm-pool policy per-AZ 3) add metrics for per-rack NIC saturation to console.

jon: logging these to eng-platform backlog. assigning priority P2 for scheduler heuristic work.

maria: closing thread for now, will update after 6h canary. thanks team. :tada:
